claim: Postpositive adjectives in this class are said to require a superlative or only.
evidence_summary: CGEL gives the money available elsewhere. The Congressional Record supplies every effort possible.
finding: Qualify the licensing condition by adjective and construction.
inference: Is a superlative or only necessary to license these adjectives in postpositive position?

evidence.source: U.S. Senate, Congressional Record (24 April 1998). S. Res. 216.
evidence.passage: §14.2, p. 445, after [12i]. CGEL requires “an attributive superlative or only” for postpositive adjectives of the class exemplified by suitable and possible. Compare the money available on p. 57.
evidence.example: The resolution uses every effort possible with neither only nor an attributive superlative.
evidence.establishes: A pre-2002 counterexample for possible after every. Different adjectives and postpositive constructions may have different licensing conditions.
evidence.locator: P. S3593, right column, resolved clause (3). PDF p. 33.
